subject: Question about the line-transect using program-DISTANCE

messages.author: 8ec137645c36c4af
messages.subject: Question about the line-transect using program-DISTANCE
parts:
Dear all Distance-users

Now I want to estimate the density of drifting seaweeds by line transect
with program-DISTANCE. The data of mine, however, are NOT parallel. The
lines form triangle, square, and etc. Is it possible that I estimate the
density almost accurately with program-DISTANCE? And how do I estimate the
density using NOT parallel transect?

Regard,

Daisuke

Ocean Research Institute

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Question about the line-transect using program-DISTANCE
parts:
Hi Daisuke, list,

There is no requirement that the lines should be parallel. See Introduction to
Distance Sampling, section 7.2.1 for a discussion of this, and Figure 7.3 for some
examples of square transects. There can be some issues with what to do at the
corners -- see the above section and Figure 7.4.

If each each sampler (square, triangle, etc) is placed at random (or, better,
systematic random) then each sampler should be treated as 1 transect in Distance
(ie line length for a square sampler would be the total length of the 4 sides).

- Len
